test_title: PYST 01: SSC Stenographer - General Awareness (Held On: 10 Dec 2024 - Shift 1)
subject: gk
question:
Select the correct alternative on the given statements based on Ashoka’s Lion capital and India’s State Emblem.

Statement I: In the original Ashoka’s Lion Capital, there are four lions mounted backto-back on a circular abacus that itself rests on a bell-shaped lotus.

Statement II: The State Emblem is an adaptation of the Lion Capital of Asoka at Sarnath in which the bell-shaped lotus was omitted.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Neither Statement I nor Statement II is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both Statement I and Statement II are true.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The original Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath features four lions standing back-to-back.
 
• The lions are mounted on a circular abacus, which in turn rests on a bell-shaped lotus.
 
• The State Emblem of India is an adaptation of the Lion Capital of Ashoka.
 
• In the State Emblem, the bell-shaped lotus was omitted, and only the abacus and the four lions were retained.
 
• The adaptation of the Lion Capital as the State Emblem signifies the Republic of India's commitment to peace and goodwill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lion Capital of Ashoka:**

 
 
• The Lion Capital was originally erected around 250 BCE by Emperor Ashoka to commemorate his conversion to Buddhism.
 
• It was discovered by archaeologists in 1905-1906 at Sarnath, near Varanasi.
 
 
 
• **Symbolism:**
 
 
• The four lions represent power, courage, confidence, and pride.
 
• The wheel (Dharma Chakra) depicted on the abacus symbolizes the eternal wheel of law.
 
 
 
• **State Emblem of India:**
 
 
• Adopted on 26th January 1950, the day India became a republic.
 
• The State Emblem also includes the motto "Satyameva Jayate" (Truth Alone Triumphs) inscribed below the abacus in Devanagari script.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Significance:**
 
 
• The bell-shaped lotus is a common feature in Mauryan architecture and represents purity and beauty.
 
• The adaptation of the Lion Capital without the lotus signifies a focus on the symbolic values of the lions and the wheel.
